questions.text:
Consider the relation R on the set $\{-2,-1,0,1,2\}$ defined by $(a,b)\in R$ if and only if $1+ab>0$. Then, among the statements :
I. The number of elements in R is 17
II. R is an equivalence relation
options: Both I and II are true
Neither I nor II is true
questions.sol:
$1+ab>0 \iff ab\ge 0$ (as $ab$ is an integer).
Pairs with $ab<0$: $a,b$ non-zero with opposite signs: $2\cdot2\cdot2=8$ pairs. So $|R|=25-8=17$: I is true.
$R$ is reflexive ($1+a^2>0$) and symmetric, but $(1,0),(0,-1)\in R$ while $(1,-1)\notin R$ ($1-1=0$). Not transitive, so II is false.
Only I is true.

questions.text: The number of values of $z\in\mathbb{C}$, satisfying the equations $$|z-(4+8i)|=\sqrt{10} \text{ and } |z-(3+5i)|+|z-(5+11i)|=4\sqrt{5},$$ is :
questions.sol:
The first is a circle with centre $(4,8)$ and radius $\sqrt{10}$.
The second is an ellipse with foci $(3,5)$, $(5,11)$: centre $(4,8)$, $2a=4\sqrt5$, $2c=\sqrt{4+36}=2\sqrt{10}$.
So $a^2=20$, $c^2=10$, $b^2=a^2-c^2=10$, i.e. $b=\sqrt{10}$.
The circle has the same centre and radius equal to the semi-minor axis, so it touches the ellipse only at the two ends of the minor axis.
Number of values $=2$.

questions.text:
If the system of linear equations :
$x+y+z=6,$
$x+2y+5z=10,$
$2x+3y+\lambda z=\mu$
has infinitely many solutions, then the value of $\lambda+\mu$ equals :
questions.sol:
$\Delta=\begin{vmatrix}1&1&1\\1&2&5\\2&3&\lambda\end{vmatrix}=(2\lambda-15)-(\lambda-10)+(3-4)=\lambda-6=0\Rightarrow\lambda=6$.
Then the third left side is the sum of the first two: $2x+3y+6z=6+10=16$, so for infinitely many solutions $\mu=16$.
$\lambda+\mu=22$.

questions.text: Let $A=\begin{bmatrix}\alpha&1&2\\2&3&0\\0&4&5\end{bmatrix}$ and $B=\begin{bmatrix}1&0&0\\0&-5\alpha&0\\0&4\alpha&-2\alpha\end{bmatrix}+\operatorname{adj}(A)$. If $\det(B)=66$, then $\det(\operatorname{adj}(A))$ equals :
questions.sol:
Cofactors of $A$ give $\operatorname{adj}(A)=\begin{bmatrix}15&3&-6\\-10&5\alpha&4\\8&-4\alpha&3\alpha-2\end{bmatrix}$.
So $B=\begin{bmatrix}16&3&-6\\-10&0&4\\8&0&\alpha-2\end{bmatrix}$.
Expanding along the second column: $\det B=-3\left[-10(\alpha-2)-32\right]=30\alpha+36=66\Rightarrow\alpha=1$.
$\det A=15\alpha+6=21$, so $\det(\operatorname{adj}A)=(\det A)^2=441$.

questions.text: Let $\alpha=3+4+8+9+13+14+\ldots$ upto 40 terms. If $(\tan\beta)^{\frac{\alpha}{1020}}$ is a root of the equation $x^2+x-2=0$, $\beta\in\left(0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, then $\sin^2\beta+3\cos^2\beta$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
The terms pair up as $(5k+3)+(5k+4)=10k+7$, $k=0,1,\ldots,19$.
$\alpha=10\cdot190+7\cdot20=2040$, so $\dfrac{\alpha}{1020}=2$.
Roots of $x^2+x-2=0$ are $1,-2$; $\tan^2\beta\ge0$ so $\tan^2\beta=1$, $\beta=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$.
$\sin^2\beta+3\cos^2\beta=\dfrac12+\dfrac32=2$.

questions.text: A candidate has to go to the examination centre to appear in an examination. The candidate uses only one means of transportation for the entire distance out of bus, scooter and car. The probabilities of the candidate going by bus, scooter and car, respectively, are $\dfrac{2}{5}$, $\dfrac{1}{5}$ and $\dfrac{2}{5}$. The probabilities that the candidate reaches late at the examination centre are $\dfrac{1}{5}$, $\dfrac{1}{3}$ and $\dfrac{1}{4}$ if the candidate uses bus, scooter and car, respectively. Given that the candidate reached late at the examination centre, the probability that the candidate travelled by bus is :
questions.sol:
$P(\text{late})=\dfrac25\cdot\dfrac15+\dfrac15\cdot\dfrac13+\dfrac25\cdot\dfrac14=\dfrac{12+10+15}{150}=\dfrac{37}{150}$.
By Bayes' theorem, $P(\text{bus}\mid\text{late})=\dfrac{12/150}{37/150}=\dfrac{12}{37}$.

questions.text: A person has three different bags and four different books. The number of ways, in which he can put these books in the bags so that no bag is empty, is :
questions.sol:
Count onto maps from 4 books to 3 bags: $3^4-\binom31 2^4+\binom32 1^4=81-48+3=36$.
(Equivalently: choose the pair of books that share a bag, $\binom42=6$, then arrange 3 groups in 3 bags, $3!=6$: $36$.)

questions.text: If a straight line drawn through the point of intersection of the lines $4x+3y-1=0$ and $3x+4y-1=0$, meets the co-ordinate axes at the points P and Q, then the locus of the mid point of PQ is :
questions.sol:
Solving, the lines meet at $\left(\dfrac17,\dfrac17\right)$.
If the mid point of PQ is $(h,k)$, then P $=(2h,0)$, Q $=(0,2k)$ and the line is $\dfrac{x}{2h}+\dfrac{y}{2k}=1$.
It passes through $\left(\dfrac17,\dfrac17\right)$: $\dfrac1{14h}+\dfrac1{14k}=1\Rightarrow h+k=14hk$.
Locus: $x+y-14xy=0$.

questions.text: Let O be the vertex of the parabola $y^2=4x$ and its chords OP and OQ are perpendicular to each other. If the locus of the mid-point of the line segment PQ is a conic C, then the length of its latus rectum is :
questions.sol:
Let P $=(t_1^2,2t_1)$, Q $=(t_2^2,2t_2)$. OP $\perp$ OQ: $\dfrac2{t_1}\cdot\dfrac2{t_2}=-1\Rightarrow t_1t_2=-4$.
Mid point: $h=\dfrac{t_1^2+t_2^2}{2}$, $k=t_1+t_2$, so $t_1^2+t_2^2=k^2-2t_1t_2=k^2+8$.
$2h=k^2+8\Rightarrow y^2=2(x-4)$.
Latus rectum $=2$.

questions.text:
Let $\alpha=3\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{6}{11}\right)$ and $\beta=3\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{4}{9}\right)$, where inverse trigonometric functions take only the principal values.
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : $\cos(\alpha+\beta)>0$.
Statement II : $\cos(\alpha)<0$.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
$\dfrac12<\dfrac6{11}<\dfrac1{\sqrt2}$, so $\dfrac\pi6<\sin^{-1}\dfrac6{11}<\dfrac\pi4$ and $\dfrac\pi2<\alpha<\dfrac{3\pi}4$. Hence $\cos\alpha<0$: Statement II is true.
$\cos\dfrac{5\pi}{12}\approx0.26<\dfrac49<\dfrac12$, so $\dfrac\pi3<\cos^{-1}\dfrac49<\dfrac{5\pi}{12}$ and $\pi<\beta<\dfrac{5\pi}4$.
Then $\dfrac{3\pi}2<\alpha+\beta<2\pi$, so $\cos(\alpha+\beta)>0$: Statement I is true.
Both statements are true.

questions.text:
For the function $f(x)=e^{\sin|x|}-|x|$, $x\in\mathbf{R}$, consider the following statements :
Statement I : $f$ is differentiable for all $x\in\mathbf{R}$.
Statement II : $f$ is increasing in $\left(-\pi,-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
For $x>0$: $f'(x)=e^{\sin x}\cos x-1\to0$ as $x\to0^+$. For $x<0$: $f(x)=e^{-\sin x}+x$, $f'(x)=1-e^{-\sin x}\cos x\to0$ as $x\to0^-$.
Both one-sided derivatives at $0$ are $0$, and $f$ is differentiable elsewhere: Statement I is true.
On $\left(-\pi,-\dfrac\pi2\right)$, $\cos x<0$, so $f'(x)=1-e^{-\sin x}\cos x>0$: $f$ is increasing, Statement II is true.
Both statements are true.

questions.text: Let $\vec{a}=4\hat{i}-\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$, $\vec{b}=10\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}$ and a vector $\vec{c}$ be such that $2\left(\vec{a}\times\vec{b}\right)+3\left(\vec{b}\times\vec{c}\right)=\vec{0}$. If $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{c}=15$, then $\vec{c}\cdot\left(\hat{i}+\hat{j}-3\hat{k}\right)$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$2(\vec a\times\vec b)+3(\vec b\times\vec c)=\vec b\times(3\vec c-2\vec a)=\vec 0$, so $3\vec c=2\vec a+\lambda\vec b$.
$\vec a\cdot\vec a=26$, $\vec a\cdot\vec b=40-2-3=35$. Then $3\vec a\cdot\vec c=52+35\lambda=45\Rightarrow\lambda=-\dfrac15$.
With $\vec d=\hat i+\hat j-3\hat k$: $\vec a\cdot\vec d=4-1-9=-6$, $\vec b\cdot\vec d=10+2+3=15$.
$\vec c\cdot\vec d=\dfrac{2(-6)-\frac15(15)}{3}=\dfrac{-15}{3}=-5$.

questions.text: Let the foot of perpendicular from the point $(\lambda,2,3)$ on the line $\dfrac{x-4}{1}=\dfrac{y-9}{2}=\dfrac{z-5}{1}$ be the point $(1,\mu,2)$. Then the distance between the lines $\dfrac{x-1}{2}=\dfrac{y-2}{3}=\dfrac{z+4}{6}$ and $\dfrac{x-\lambda}{2}=\dfrac{y-\mu}{3}=\dfrac{z+5}{6}$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
A point of the line is $(4+t,9+2t,5+t)$; $x=1$ gives $t=-3$, so the foot is $(1,3,2)$ and $\mu=3$.
Perpendicularity: $(\lambda-1,\,2-3,\,3-2)\cdot(1,2,1)=\lambda-1-2+1=0\Rightarrow\lambda=2$.
The lines are parallel with direction $(2,3,6)$, $|\vec d|=7$, through $(1,2,-4)$ and $(2,3,-5)$.
Joining vector $(1,1,-1)$; $(1,1,-1)\times(2,3,6)=(9,-8,1)$, of length $\sqrt{146}$.
Distance $=\dfrac{\sqrt{146}}{7}$.

questions.text: The value of the integral $\displaystyle\int_0^2\dfrac{\sqrt{x\left(x^2+x+1\right)}}{\left(\sqrt{x+1}\right)\left(\sqrt{x^4+x^2+1}\right)}\,dx$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$x^4+x^2+1=(x^2+x+1)(x^2-x+1)$, so the integrand is $\dfrac{\sqrt x}{\sqrt{(x+1)(x^2-x+1)}}=\dfrac{\sqrt x}{\sqrt{1+x^3}}$.
Put $t=x^{3/2}$, $dt=\dfrac32\sqrt x\,dx$: $I=\dfrac23\displaystyle\int_0^{2\sqrt2}\dfrac{dt}{\sqrt{1+t^2}}=\dfrac23\left[\ln\left(t+\sqrt{1+t^2}\right)\right]_0^{2\sqrt2}$.
$I=\dfrac23\log_e\left(2\sqrt2+3\right)$.

questions.text: Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation $$x\sqrt{1-x^2}\,dy+\left(y\sqrt{1-x^2}-x\cos^{-1}x\right)dx=0,\ x\in(0,1),\ \lim_{x\to1^-}y(x)=1.$$ Then $y\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$ equals :
questions.sol:
$\dfrac{dy}{dx}+\dfrac yx=\dfrac{\cos^{-1}x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}$; integrating factor $x$: $\dfrac{d(xy)}{dx}=\dfrac{x\cos^{-1}x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}$.
With $x=\cos u$: $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{x\cos^{-1}x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}dx=-\int u\cos u\,du=-(u\sin u+\cos u)$.
So $xy=-\sqrt{1-x^2}\cos^{-1}x-x+C$. As $x\to1^-$: $1=-1+C\Rightarrow C=2$.
At $x=\dfrac12$: $\dfrac y2=-\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\cdot\dfrac\pi3-\dfrac12+2$, so $y=3-\dfrac{\pi}{\sqrt3}$.

questions.text: Let $f:(1,\infty)\to\mathbf{R}$ be a function defined as $f(x)=\dfrac{x-1}{x+1}$. Let $f^{i+1}(x)=f\left(f^{i}(x)\right)$, $i=1,2,\ldots,25$, where $f^1(x)=f(x)$. If $g(x)+f^{26}(x)=0$, $x\in(1,\infty)$, then the area of the region bounded by the curves $y=g(x)$, $2y=2x-3$, $y=0$ and $x=4$ is :
questions.sol:
$f^2(x)=\dfrac{\frac{x-1}{x+1}-1}{\frac{x-1}{x+1}+1}=-\dfrac1x$, so $f^4(x)=x$ and $f^{26}=f^2$. Hence $g(x)=\dfrac1x$.
$y=\dfrac1x$ meets $y=x-\dfrac32$ at $x=2$; the line meets $y=0$ at $x=\dfrac32$.
The region lies under the line for $\dfrac32\le x\le2$ and under $y=\dfrac1x$ for $2\le x\le4$.
Area $=\displaystyle\int_{3/2}^{2}\left(x-\dfrac32\right)dx+\int_2^4\dfrac{dx}{x}=\dfrac18+\log_e2$.

questions.text: Let $f(x)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{1}{3}, & x\le\dfrac{\pi}{2}\\[2mm] \dfrac{b(1-\sin x)}{(\pi-2x)^2}, & x>\dfrac{\pi}{2}\end{cases}$. If $f$ is continuous at $x=\pi/2$, then the value of $\displaystyle\int_0^{3b-6}\left|x^2+2x-3\right|dx$ is :
questions.sol:
Put $x=\dfrac\pi2+h$: $\dfrac{b(1-\cos h)}{4h^2}\to\dfrac b8$. Continuity: $\dfrac b8=\dfrac13\Rightarrow b=\dfrac83$, so $3b-6=2$.
$x^2+2x-3=(x+3)(x-1)$ is negative on $(0,1)$ and positive on $(1,2)$.
$\displaystyle\int_0^1(3-2x-x^2)dx=\dfrac53$, $\displaystyle\int_1^2(x^2+2x-3)dx=\dfrac73$.
Value $=\dfrac{12}{3}=4$.

questions.text: Let $\dfrac{x^2}{f\left(a^2+7a+3\right)}+\dfrac{y^2}{f(3a+15)}=1$ represent an ellipse with major axis along $y$-axis, where $f$ is a strictly decreasing positive function on $\mathbf{R}$. If the set of all possible values of a is $\mathbf{R}-[\alpha,\beta]$, then $\alpha^2+\beta^2$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
Major axis along the $y$-axis: $f(3a+15)>f(a^2+7a+3)$.
$f$ is strictly decreasing, so $3a+15<a^2+7a+3\iff a^2+4a-12>0\iff(a+6)(a-2)>0$.
So $a\in\mathbf R-[-6,2]$ and $\alpha^2+\beta^2=36+4=40$.

questions.text: The sum of squares of all the real solutions of the equation $$\log_{(x+1)}\left(2x^2+5x+3\right)=4-\log_{(2x+3)}\left(x^2+2x+1\right)$$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
$2x^2+5x+3=(2x+3)(x+1)$ and $x^2+2x+1=(x+1)^2$. Let $t=\log_{(x+1)}(2x+3)$.
The equation becomes $1+t=4-\dfrac2t\Rightarrow t^2-3t+2=0\Rightarrow t=1$ or $2$.
$t=1$: $2x+3=x+1\Rightarrow x=-2$, rejected (base negative).
$t=2$: $2x+3=(x+1)^2\Rightarrow x^2=2$; the domain needs $x>-1$, $x\ne0$, so $x=\sqrt2$ only.
Sum of squares $=2$.

questions.text: If $\displaystyle\int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/4}\left(\cot\left(x-\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)\cot\left(x+\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)+1\right)dx=\alpha\log_e\left(\sqrt{3}-1\right)$, then $9\alpha^2$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
Let $A=x-\dfrac\pi3$, $B=x+\dfrac\pi3$, so $B-A=\dfrac{2\pi}3$ and $\cot(B-A)=\dfrac{\cot A\cot B+1}{\cot A-\cot B}$.
Hence $\cot A\cot B+1=-\dfrac1{\sqrt3}(\cot A-\cot B)$, and the integral is $-\dfrac1{\sqrt3}\left[\ln\left|\dfrac{\sin(x-\pi/3)}{\sin(x+\pi/3)}\right|\right]_{\pi/6}^{\pi/4}$.
At $\dfrac\pi4$: $\dfrac{\sin15^\circ}{\sin105^\circ}=\dfrac{\sqrt3-1}{\sqrt3+1}=2-\sqrt3$. At $\dfrac\pi6$: $\dfrac{1/2}{1}=\dfrac12$.
Integral $=-\dfrac1{\sqrt3}\ln\left(2(2-\sqrt3)\right)=-\dfrac1{\sqrt3}\ln(\sqrt3-1)^2=-\dfrac2{\sqrt3}\ln(\sqrt3-1)$.
$\alpha=-\dfrac2{\sqrt3}$, so $9\alpha^2=12$.

questions.text:
Let a line $L_1$ pass through the origin and be perpendicular to the lines
$L_2:\ \vec{r}=(3+t)\hat{i}+(2t-1)\hat{j}+(2t+4)\hat{k}$ and
$L_3:\ \vec{r}=(3+2s)\hat{i}+(3+2s)\hat{j}+(2+s)\hat{k}$, $t,s\in\mathbf{R}$.
If $(a,b,c)$, $a\in\mathbf{Z}$, is the point on $L_3$ at a distance of $\sqrt{17}$ from the point of intersection of $L_1$ and $L_2$, then $(a+b+c)^2$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
Directions: $L_2$: $(1,2,2)$, $L_3$: $(2,2,1)$; their cross product is $(-2,3,-2)$, the direction of $L_1$.
$L_1\cap L_2$: $(3+t,2t-1,2t+4)=\lambda(-2,3,-2)$. The $x$ and $z$ equations give $3+t=2t+4\Rightarrow t=-1$, point $(2,-3,2)$ ($\lambda=-1$, consistent).
Point on $L_3$: $(3+2s,3+2s,2+s)$; distance$^2$: $(1+2s)^2+(6+2s)^2+s^2=17\Rightarrow9s^2+28s+20=0$.
$s=-2$ or $s=-\dfrac{10}9$; $a\in\mathbf Z$ needs $s=-2$: point $(-1,-1,0)$.
$(a+b+c)^2=4$.

questions.text: Consider the circle $C: x^2+y^2-6x-8y-11=0$. Let a variable chord AB of the circle C subtend a right angle at the origin. If the locus of the foot of the perpendicular drawn from the origin on the chord AB is the circle $x^2+y^2-\alpha x-\beta y-\gamma=0$, then $\alpha+\beta+2\gamma$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
Let the foot be $(h,k)$; chord AB: $hx+ky=h^2+k^2$.
Homogenise the circle with $\dfrac{hx+ky}{h^2+k^2}=1$: $x^2+y^2-(6x+8y)\dfrac{hx+ky}{h^2+k^2}-11\dfrac{(hx+ky)^2}{(h^2+k^2)^2}=0$.
Right angle at O: sum of the coefficients of $x^2$ and $y^2$ is $0$: $2-\dfrac{6h+8k}{h^2+k^2}-\dfrac{11}{h^2+k^2}=0$.
Locus: $x^2+y^2-3x-4y-\dfrac{11}2=0$, so $\alpha=3$, $\beta=4$, $\gamma=\dfrac{11}2$.
$\alpha+\beta+2\gamma=18$.

questions.text: Let $f$ be a polynomial function such that $$\log_2(f(x))=\left(\log_2\left(2+\dfrac{2}{3}+\dfrac{2}{9}+\ldots\infty\right)\right)\cdot\log_3\left(1+\dfrac{f(x)}{f\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)}\right),\ x>0$$ and $f(6)=37$. Then $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{10}f(n)$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
$2+\dfrac23+\dfrac29+\ldots=\dfrac{2}{1-\frac13}=3$, so the right side is $\log_2 3\cdot\log_3\left(1+\dfrac{f(x)}{f(1/x)}\right)=\log_2\left(1+\dfrac{f(x)}{f(1/x)}\right)$.
Hence $f(x)=1+\dfrac{f(x)}{f(1/x)}$, i.e. $f(x)f(1/x)=f(x)+f(1/x)$, so $f(x)=1\pm x^n$.
$f(6)=37=1+6^2$ gives $f(x)=x^2+1$.
$\sum_{n=1}^{10}(n^2+1)=385+10=395$.

questions.text:
Consider the equation $H=\dfrac{x^p\epsilon^q E^r}{t^s}$
Where $H=$ magnetic field; $E=$ electric field, $\epsilon=$ permittivity, $x=$ distance, $t=$ time
The values of $p$, $q$, $r$ and $s$ respectively are :
questions.sol:
$[H]=\text{A L}^{-1}$, $[\epsilon]=\text{M}^{-1}\text{L}^{-3}\text{T}^4\text{A}^2$, $[E]=\text{M L T}^{-3}\text{A}^{-1}$.
Compare powers: M: $-q+r=0$; L: $p-3q+r=-1$; T: $4q-3r-s=0$; A: $2q-r=1$.
These give $q=r=1$, $s=1$, $p=1$.
(Check: $\dfrac{x\,\epsilon E}{t}$ has units $\dfrac{\text{m}\cdot\text{C m}^{-2}}{\text{s}}=\text{A m}^{-1}$, as in $\oint H\,dl=\epsilon\dfrac{d\Phi_E}{dt}$.)
So $p,q,r,s=1,1,1,1$.

questions.text: A car moving with a speed of 54 km/h takes a turn of radius 20 m. A simple pendulum is suspended from the ceiling of the car. Determine the angle made by the string of the pendulum with the vertical during the turning. (Take $g=10\ \text{m/s}^2$)
questions.sol:
$v=54$ km/h $=15$ m/s; centripetal acceleration $\dfrac{v^2}{r}=\dfrac{225}{20}=11.25\ \text{m/s}^2$.
In the car frame the bob is in equilibrium: $\tan\theta=\dfrac{v^2/r}{g}=\dfrac{11.25}{10}=1.125$.
$\theta=\tan^{-1}(1.125)$.

questions.text: A gas balloon is going up with a constant velocity of 10 m/s. When this balloon reached a height of 75 m, a stone is dropped from it and balloon keeps moving up with the same velocity. The height of the balloon when the stone hits the ground is __________ m. (Take $g=10\ \text{m/s}^2$)
questions.sol:
The stone starts with $10$ m/s upward from 75 m: $-75=10t-5t^2\Rightarrow t^2-2t-15=0\Rightarrow t=5$ s.
In 5 s the balloon rises $10\times5=50$ m more.
Height of the balloon $=75+50=125$ m.

questions.text: A thin biconvex lens is prepared from the glass $(\mu=1.5)$ both curved surfaces of which have equal radii of 20 cm each. Left side surface of the lens is silvered from outside to make it reflecting. To have the position of image and object at the same place, the object should be placed, from the lens at a distance of __________ cm.
questions.sol:
Lens: $\dfrac1{f_L}=(1.5-1)\left(\dfrac1{20}+\dfrac1{20}\right)=\dfrac1{20}$, so $f_L=20$ cm. Silvered surface: concave mirror with $f_m=\dfrac R2=10$ cm.
Power of the system: $P=2P_L+P_m=\dfrac2{20}+\dfrac1{10}=\dfrac15$, so it acts as a concave mirror of focal length $F=5$ cm.
Image coincides with the object when the object is at the centre of curvature: $2F=10$ cm.

questions.text: Two identical bodies, projected with the same speed at two different angles cover the same horizontal range $R$. If the time of flight of these bodies are 5 s and 10 s, respectively, then the value of $R$ is __________ m. (Take $g=10\ \text{m/s}^2$)
questions.sol:
Equal ranges need complementary angles $\theta$ and $90^\circ-\theta$: $T_1=\dfrac{2u\sin\theta}{g}$, $T_2=\dfrac{2u\cos\theta}{g}$.
$T_1T_2=\dfrac{2u^2\sin2\theta}{g^2}=\dfrac{2R}{g}$.
$R=\dfrac{gT_1T_2}{2}=\dfrac{10\times5\times10}{2}=250$ m.

questions.text: A solid cylinder having radius $R$ and length $L$ is slipping on a rough horizontal plane. At time $t=0$ the cylinder has a translational velocity $v_o=49$ m/s, perpendicular to its axis and a rotational velocity $v_o/4R$ about the centre. The time taken by the cylinder to start rolling is __________ seconds. (coefficient of kinetic friction $\mu_K=0.25$ and $g=9.8\ \text{m/s}^2$)
questions.sol:
Since $v_o>\omega_oR$, kinetic friction $\mu_Kmg$ acts backwards: $v=v_o-\mu_Kgt$.
Its torque speeds up the rotation: $\alpha=\dfrac{\mu_KmgR}{\frac12mR^2}=\dfrac{2\mu_Kg}{R}$, so $\omega R=\dfrac{v_o}{4}+2\mu_Kgt$.
Rolling starts when $v=\omega R$: $v_o-\dfrac{v_o}4=3\mu_Kgt\Rightarrow t=\dfrac{v_o}{4\mu_Kg}=\dfrac{49}{4\times0.25\times9.8}=5$ s.

questions.text: A liquid of density $600\ \text{kg/m}^3$ flowing steadily in a tube of varying cross-section. The cross-section at a point $A$ is $1.0\ \text{cm}^2$ and that at $B$ is $20\ \text{mm}^2$. Both the points $A$ and $B$ are in same horizontal plane, the speed of the liquid at $A$ is 10 cm/s. The difference in pressures at $A$ and $B$ points is __________ Pa.
questions.sol:
Continuity: $v_B=v_A\dfrac{A_A}{A_B}=0.1\times\dfrac{100}{20}=0.5$ m/s.
Bernoulli (same level): $P_A-P_B=\dfrac12\rho\left(v_B^2-v_A^2\right)=\dfrac12\times600\times(0.25-0.01)=72$ Pa.

questions.text: A spherical liquid drop of radius $R$ acquires the terminal velocity $v_1$ when falls through a gas of viscosity $\eta$. Now the drop is broken into 64 identical droplets and each droplet acquires terminal velocity $v_2$ falling through the same gas. The ratio of terminal velocities $v_1/v_2$ is __________.
questions.sol:
Volume is conserved: $64r^3=R^3\Rightarrow r=\dfrac R4$.
Terminal velocity $v=\dfrac{2r^2(\rho-\sigma)g}{9\eta}\propto r^2$.
$\dfrac{v_1}{v_2}=\left(\dfrac Rr\right)^2=16$.

questions.text: One mole of diatomic gas having rotational modes only is kept in a cylinder with a piston system. The cross-section area of the cylinder is $4\ \text{cm}^2$. The gas is heated slowly to raise the temperature by $1.2\ {}^\circ\text{C}$ during which the piston moves by 25 mm. The amount of heat supplied to the gas is __________ J. (Atmospheric pressure $=100$ kPa, $R=8.3$ J/mol.K) (Neglect mass of the piston)
questions.note: Official final key: (1) or (2) (either option is awarded marks).
questions.sol:
Translational and rotational modes only: $C_v=\dfrac52R$, so $\Delta U=nC_v\Delta T=1\times\dfrac52\times8.3\times1.2=24.9$ J.
Work against the atmosphere: $W=P\,A\,x=10^5\times4\times10^{-4}\times0.025=1$ J.
The data are not consistent with each other (for 1 mol at constant pressure $P\Delta V$ should equal $nR\Delta T\approx10$ J), so $Q=\Delta U+W$ does not give a listed value exactly. The intended answer is the heat $\approx nC_v\Delta T\approx25$ J.
The official final key accepts both $24.8$ and $25$.

questions.text: Initial pressure and volume of a monoatomic ideal gas are $P$ and $V$. The change in internal energy of this gas in adiabatic expansion to volume $V_{final}=27\,V$ is __________ J.
questions.sol:
Monoatomic: $\gamma=\dfrac53$, $TV^{2/3}=$ constant, so $T_f=T\left(\dfrac1{27}\right)^{2/3}=\dfrac T9$.
$\Delta U=\dfrac32nR(T_f-T)=\dfrac32PV\left(\dfrac19-1\right)=-\dfrac43PV$.

questions.text: The frequency of oscillation of a mass $m$ suspended by a spring is $v_1$. If the length of the spring is cut to half, the same mass oscillates with frequency $v_2$. The value of $v_2/v_1$ is __________.
questions.sol:
Spring constant $\propto\dfrac1{\text{length}}$, so halving the length doubles $k$.
$v=\dfrac1{2\pi}\sqrt{\dfrac km}\propto\sqrt k$, hence $\dfrac{v_2}{v_1}=\sqrt2$.

questions.text: A monochromatic source of light operating at 15 kW emits $2.5\times10^{22}$ photons/s. The region of an electromagnetic spectrum to which the emitted electromagnetic radiation belongs to __________. (Take $h=6.6\times10^{-34}$ J.s and $c=3\times10^8$ m/s).
questions.sol:
Energy per photon $E=\dfrac{15\times10^3}{2.5\times10^{22}}=6\times10^{-19}$ J.
$\lambda=\dfrac{hc}{E}=\dfrac{6.6\times10^{-34}\times3\times10^8}{6\times10^{-19}}=3.3\times10^{-7}$ m $=330$ nm.
This lies in the ultraviolet region.

questions.text: A current carrying circular loop of radius 2 cm with unit normal $\hat{n}=\dfrac{\hat{k}+\hat{i}}{\sqrt{2}}$ is placed in a magnetic field, $\vec{B}=B_o\left(3\hat{i}+2\hat{k}\right)$. If $B_o=4\times10^{-3}$ T and current $I=100\sqrt{2}$ A, the torque experienced by the loop is __________ Wb.A. $(\pi=3.14)$
questions.sol:
$\vec m=I\pi r^2\hat n=100\sqrt2\times3.14\times4\times10^{-4}\times\dfrac{\hat i+\hat k}{\sqrt2}=0.1256\,(\hat i+\hat k)$.
$\vec\tau=\vec m\times\vec B=0.1256\times4\times10^{-3}\,(\hat i+\hat k)\times(3\hat i+2\hat k)$.
$(\hat i+\hat k)\times(3\hat i+2\hat k)=-2\hat j+3\hat j=\hat j$.
$\vec\tau=5.024\times10^{-4}\,\hat j=5024\times10^{-7}\,\hat j$.

questions.text: A 30 cm long solenoid has 10 turns per cm and area of $5\ \text{cm}^2$. The current through the solenoid coil varies from 2 A to 4 A in 3.14 s. The e.m.f. induced in the coil is $\alpha\times10^{-5}$ V. The value $\alpha$ is __________.
questions.sol:
$n=1000$ turns/m, $l=0.3$ m, $A=5\times10^{-4}\ \text{m}^2$.
$L=\mu_0n^2Al=4\pi\times10^{-7}\times10^6\times5\times10^{-4}\times0.3=6\pi\times10^{-5}$ H.
$\varepsilon=L\dfrac{\Delta I}{\Delta t}=6\pi\times10^{-5}\times\dfrac{2}{3.14}=12\times10^{-5}$ V, so $\alpha=12$.

questions.text: Two point charges $q_1=3\ \mu C$ and $q_2=-4\ \mu C$ are placed at points $\left(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\right)$ and $\left(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}\right)$ respectively. Force on charge $q_2$ is __________ N. $\left(\text{Take } \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}=9\times10^9 \text{ SI Units}\right)$
questions.sol:
$\vec r=\vec r_2-\vec r_1=-\hat i-2\hat j-2\hat k$, $|\vec r|=3$ m.
$\vec F_2=\dfrac{kq_1q_2}{r^3}\vec r=\dfrac{9\times10^9\times3\times10^{-6}\times(-4\times10^{-6})}{27}(-\hat i-2\hat j-2\hat k)$.
$\vec F_2=-0.004\,(-\hat i-2\hat j-2\hat k)=\left(4\hat i+8\hat j+8\hat k\right)\times10^{-3}$ N (attraction, towards $q_1$).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Light ray incident along a vector $\vec{AO}$ $\left(\vec{AO}=2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}\right)$ emerges out along vector $\vec{OB}$ $\left(\vec{OB}=C\hat{i}-4\hat{j}\right)$ as shown in the figure below. The value of $C$ is __________.
questions.sol:
Angles are measured from the normal (the $y$-axis): $\sin\alpha=\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{13}}$, $\sin\beta=\dfrac{C}{\sqrt{C^2+16}}$.
Snell's law: $1\times\dfrac2{\sqrt{13}}=1.5\,\dfrac{C}{\sqrt{C^2+16}}\Rightarrow\dfrac4{13}=\dfrac{2.25C^2}{C^2+16}$.
$4C^2+64=29.25C^2\Rightarrow C^2=\dfrac{64}{25.25}\approx2.53\Rightarrow C\approx1.6$.

questions.text: $K_1$ and $K_2$ be the maximum kinetic energies of photoelectrons emitted from a surface of a given material for the light of wavelength $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_2$, respectively. If $\lambda_1=2\lambda_2$ then the work function of material is given by :
questions.sol:
$K_1=\dfrac{hc}{\lambda_1}-\phi$ and $K_2=\dfrac{hc}{\lambda_2}-\phi=\dfrac{2hc}{\lambda_1}-\phi$.
So $K_2=2(K_1+\phi)-\phi=2K_1+\phi$.
$\phi=K_2-2K_1$.

questions.text: Two radioactive substances A and B of mass numbers 200 and 212 respectively, shows spontaneous $\alpha$-decay with same $Q$ value of 1 MeV. The ratio of energies of $\alpha$-rays produced by A and B is __________.
questions.sol:
Momentum conservation shares $Q$ so that $K_\alpha=Q\,\dfrac{A-4}{A}$.
$K_A=\dfrac{196}{200}$ MeV, $K_B=\dfrac{208}{212}$ MeV.
$\dfrac{K_A}{K_B}=\dfrac{196\times212}{200\times208}=\dfrac{41552}{41600}=\dfrac{2597}{2600}$.

questions.text: The output $Y$ for the given inputs $A$ and $B$ to the circuit is :
questions.sol:
Upper AND gate: $A\cdot B$. Lower AND gate (inverted $A$ input): $\bar A\cdot B$.
$Y=AB+\bar AB=B$.
So $Y$ follows $B$: $Y=1$ for $0<t<2$ s, $0$ for $2<t<3$ s, and $1$ again after $t=3$ s. This is option (2).

questions.text:
A parallel plate capacitor is having separation between plates 0.885 mm. It has a capacitance of $1\ \mu\text{F}$ when the space between the plates is filled with an insulating material of resistivity $1\times10^{13}\ \Omega\text{m}$ and resistance $17.7\times10^{14}\ \Omega$. Relative permittivity of the insulating material is $\alpha\times10^7$. The value of $\alpha$ is __________.
(Take permittivity of free space $=8.85\times10^{-12}$ F/m)
questions.sol:
$R=\dfrac{\rho d}{A}\Rightarrow A=\dfrac{\rho d}{R}=\dfrac{10^{13}\times0.885\times10^{-3}}{17.7\times10^{14}}=5\times10^{-6}\ \text{m}^2$.
$C=\dfrac{K\epsilon_0A}{d}\Rightarrow K=\dfrac{Cd}{\epsilon_0A}=\dfrac{10^{-6}\times0.885\times10^{-3}}{8.85\times10^{-12}\times5\times10^{-6}}=2\times10^7$.
$\alpha=2$.

questions.text: Some distant star is to be observed by some telescope of diameter of objective lens $a$, at an angular resolution of $3.0\times10^{-7}$ radian. If the wavelength of light from the star reaching the telescope is 500 nm, the minimum diameter of the objective lens of the telescope is __________ cm. (nearest integer)
questions.sol:
Limit of resolution: $\Delta\theta=\dfrac{1.22\lambda}{a}$.
$a=\dfrac{1.22\times500\times10^{-9}}{3.0\times10^{-7}}=2.033$ m $\approx203$ cm.

questions.text: A 5 mg particle carrying a charge of $5\pi\times10^{-6}$ C is moving with velocity of $\left(3\hat{i}+2\hat{k}\right)\times10^{-2}$ m/s in a region having magnetic field $\vec{B}=0.1\,\hat{k}\ \text{Wb/m}^2$. It moves a distance of $\alpha$ meter along $\hat{k}$ when it completes 5 revolutions. The value of $\alpha$ is __________.
questions.sol:
The path is a helix about $\hat k$. Period $T=\dfrac{2\pi m}{qB}=\dfrac{2\pi\times5\times10^{-6}}{5\pi\times10^{-6}\times0.1}=20$ s.
Velocity along $\hat k$ is unchanged: $2\times10^{-2}$ m/s.
5 revolutions take 100 s, so $\alpha=2\times10^{-2}\times100=2$ m.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The stored charge in the capacitor in steady state of the following circuit is __________ $\mu$C.
questions.sol:
In steady state no current flows through the capacitor branch (or its $10\ \Omega$), so the capacitor voltage equals the voltage across the right-hand $4\ \Omega$.
Right section: $4+4+2=10\ \Omega$, in parallel with the $10\ \Omega$: $5\ \Omega$. Adding $5+2$: $12\ \Omega$ in total, connected directly across the 12 V cell (in parallel with the $12\ \Omega$).
Current into this ladder $=\dfrac{12}{12}=1$ A; voltage across the $10\ \Omega$ $=1\times5=5$ V.
Current in the right section $=\dfrac5{10}=0.5$ A, so the voltage across the $4\ \Omega$ $=2$ V.
$Q=CV=100\ \mu\text{F}\times2\ \text{V}=200\ \mu$C.

questions.text: Two masses of 3.4 kg and 2.5 kg are accelerated from an initial speed of 5 m/s and 12 m/s, respectively. The distances traversed by the masses in the $5^{\text{th}}$ second are 104 m and 129 m, respectively. The ratio of their momenta after 10 s is $\dfrac{x}{8}$. The value of $x$ is __________.
questions.sol:
Distance in the $n^{\text{th}}$ second: $s_n=u+\dfrac a2(2n-1)$.
$104=5+4.5a_1\Rightarrow a_1=22\ \text{m/s}^2$; $129=12+4.5a_2\Rightarrow a_2=26\ \text{m/s}^2$.
After 10 s: $v_1=5+220=225$ m/s, $v_2=12+260=272$ m/s.
$\dfrac{p_1}{p_2}=\dfrac{3.4\times225}{2.5\times272}=\dfrac{765}{680}=\dfrac98$, so $x=9$.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Given : Molar mass of C, H, O, Cl are 12, 1, 16 and 35.5 g mol$^{-1}$, respectively
Statement I : In 30% (w/w) solution of methanol in $\mathrm{CCl_4}$ (at T K), the mole fraction of $\mathrm{CCl_4}$ is equal to 0.33.
Statement II : Mixture of methanol and $\mathrm{CCl_4}$ shows positive deviation from Raoult's law.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

questions.text: Bromine trifluoride autoionizes to form $\mathrm{BrF_2^{\oplus}}$ and $\mathrm{BrF_4^{\ominus}}$. The shapes of the cation and anion are respectively __________, and __________.
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{BrF_2^+}$: Br has 7 − 1 = 6 valence electrons; 2 bond pairs + 2 lone pairs ($sp^3$) give a bent shape.
$\mathrm{BrF_4^-}$: 8 valence electrons; 4 bond pairs + 2 lone pairs ($sp^3d^2$) give a square planar shape.
Bent, square planar.

questions.text:
Which of the following statements are not correct ?
A. For water, magnitude of $K_b$ is more than the magnitude of $K_f$.
B. The elevation in boiling point of water when a non-volatile solute is added to it is larger in magnitude than its depression in freezing point.
C. Osmotic pressure measurement is preferred over any other colligative property to determine molar mass of proteins and polymers.
D. The dimerised form of benzoic acid in benzene is $\mathrm{C_6H_5{-}\overset{\displaystyle O}{\overset{\|}{C}}{-}OH\ \cdots\ O{=}\overset{\displaystyle OH}{\overset{|}{C}}{-}C_6H_5}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
A: for water $K_b=0.52$ and $K_f=1.86$ K kg mol$^{-1}$, so A is not correct.
B: since $K_b<K_f$, $\Delta T_b<\Delta T_f$ for the same molality, so B is not correct.
C is correct (osmotic pressure is large and measured at room temperature).
D: the benzoic acid dimer is cyclic, held by two O–H···O hydrogen bonds, not the single hydrogen bond shown, so D is not correct.
Not correct: A, B and D.

questions.text:
Consider the following reactions in which all the reactants and products are present in gaseous state
$2\,xy\rightleftharpoons x_2+y_2\quad K_1=2.5\times10^5$
$xy+\dfrac{1}{2}z_2\rightleftharpoons xyz\quad K_2=5\times10^{-3}$
The value of $K_3$ for the equilibrium $\dfrac{1}{2}x_2+\dfrac{1}{2}y_2+\dfrac{1}{2}z_2\rightleftharpoons xyz$ is :
questions.sol:
Reverse and halve the first reaction: $\dfrac12x_2+\dfrac12y_2\rightleftharpoons xy$, $K=\dfrac1{\sqrt{K_1}}=\dfrac1{500}=2\times10^{-3}$.
Add the second reaction: $K_3=2\times10^{-3}\times5\times10^{-3}=1.0\times10^{-5}$.

questions.text:
Given at 298 K : $E^{\ominus}_{\mathrm{Fe^{2+}/Fe}}=X$ Volt, $E^{\ominus}_{\mathrm{Fe^{3+}/Fe}}=Y$ Volt
The $E^{\ominus}_{\mathrm{Fe^{3+}/Fe^{2+}}}$ in Volt at 298 K is given by :
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{Fe^{3+}+3e^-\to Fe}$: $\Delta G_1^\circ=-3FY$. $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}+2e^-\to Fe}$: $\Delta G_2^\circ=-2FX$.
$\mathrm{Fe^{3+}+e^-\to Fe^{2+}}$: $\Delta G^\circ=\Delta G_1^\circ-\Delta G_2^\circ=-3FY+2FX=-FE^\circ$.
$E^\circ=3Y-2X$.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
$R=8.314\ \mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,mol^{-1}}$ and 1 cal $=4.2$ J
Statement I : When $E_a=12.6$ kcal/mol, the room temperature rate constant is doubled by a $10\ {}^\circ$C increase in temperature (298 K to 308 K)
Statement II : For a first order reactions $\mathrm{A\to B}$, the graph of $t_{1/2}$ (s) against $[\mathrm{A}]_0$ (mol L$^{-1}$) is as shown below.
Here $[\mathrm{A}]_0$ is the initial concentration of A and $t_{1/2}$ is half life of reaction.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
$E_a=12.6\times4.2=52.92$ kJ/mol. $\ln\dfrac{k_2}{k_1}=\dfrac{E_a}{R}\left(\dfrac1{298}-\dfrac1{308}\right)=\dfrac{52920}{8.314}\times\dfrac{10}{298\times308}\approx0.693$.
So $\dfrac{k_2}{k_1}\approx2$: Statement I is true.
For a first order reaction $t_{1/2}=\dfrac{0.693}{k}$ is independent of $[\mathrm A]_0$, so the graph should be a horizontal line, not a straight line through the origin: Statement II is false.

questions.text:
Find the correct statements related to group 15 hydrides.
A. Reducing nature increases from $\mathrm{NH_3}$ to $\mathrm{BiH_3}$
B. Tendency to donate lone pair of electrons decreases from $\mathrm{NH_3}$ to $\mathrm{BiH_3}$
C. The stability of hydrides decreases from $\mathrm{NH_3}$ to $\mathrm{BiH_3}$
D. HEH bond angle decreases from $\mathrm{NH_3}$ to $\mathrm{SbH_3}$ (E = Elements of group 15)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :

Down the group the E–H bond becomes longer and weaker, so thermal stability decreases (C) and reducing character increases (A).

Statement I : The number of pairs among $[\mathrm{Ti^{4+},V^{2+}}]$, $[\mathrm{V^{2+},Mn^{2+}}]$, $[\mathrm{Mn^{2+},Fe^{3+}}]$ and $[\mathrm{V^{2+},Cr^{2+}}]$ in which both ions are coloured is 3.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct from the options given below :

Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

questions.text:
Given below are two statements for catalytic properties of transition metals.
Statement I : First row transition metals which act as catalyst utilise their 3d electrons only for formation of bonds between reactant molecules and atoms on the surface of catalyst.
Statement II : There is increase in the concentration of reactants on the surface of catalyst which strengthens the bonds in reacting molecules.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol:
First row transition metals use both their 3d and 4s electrons to form bonds with the reactant molecules at the surface, so Statement I (3d only) is incorrect.
This bonding increases the concentration of reactants at the surface and weakens (not strengthens) the bonds in the reacting molecules, so Statement II is incorrect.
Both statements are incorrect.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : Vapours of the liquid with higher boiling point condense before vapours of the liquid with lower boiling points in fractional distillation.
Statement II : The vapours rising up in the fractionating column become richer in high boiling component of the mixture.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
In the fractionating column the higher boiling component condenses first and runs back, so Statement I is true.
Hence the vapours rising up become richer in the lower boiling component, so Statement II is false.

questions.text: The major product of which of the following reaction is not obtained by rearrangement reaction ?
questions.sol:
(1) The 1° propyl cation from 1-chloropropane/$\mathrm{AlCl_3}$ rearranges (hydride shift) to the 2° isopropyl cation, giving cumene: rearrangement.
(2) tert-Butyl alcohol gives the 3° tert-butyl cation directly, which loses $\mathrm{H^+}$ to give 2-methylpropene: no rearrangement.
(3) Isomerisation of n-hexane to 2-methylpentane with anhyd. $\mathrm{AlCl_3}$/HCl: rearrangement.
(4) Neopentyl-type alcohol (2,2-dimethylpropan-1-ol) gives a 1° cation that undergoes a methyl shift to a 3° cation, giving 2-methylbut-2-ene: rearrangement.
Answer: reaction (2).

questions.text: The total number of aromatic compounds/species from the following is
questions.sol:
p-Benzoquinone: the ring has no cyclic $(4n+2)\pi$ system (two C=O groups take the conjugation out of the ring): non-aromatic.
Tropylium cation: planar, $6\pi$ electrons: aromatic.
Phenanthrene: $14\pi$ electrons in a fully conjugated planar system: aromatic.
Cyclobutadienyl dication: $2\pi$ electrons ($n=0$): aromatic.
1,2-Dihydronaphthalene: the whole ring system is not continuously conjugated (two $\mathrm{sp^3}$ $\mathrm{CH_2}$ groups), and the cyclohexadienyl anion also has an $\mathrm{sp^3}$ $\mathrm{CH_2}$ in the ring: neither is counted as aromatic as a species.
Total $=3$ (as per the official key).

Statement I : Due to increase in van der Waals forces, the order of boiling points is $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2I>CH_3CH_2I>CH_3I}$.
Statement II : As p-dichlorobenzene is more symmetric, its melting point is higher than o-dichlorobenzene, however its boiling point is lower than o-dichlorobenzene (structures as shown below).
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Statement I: boiling points rise with molecular size because van der Waals forces increase: $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2I}$ (375 K) $>$ $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2I}$ (345 K) $>$ $\mathrm{CH_3I}$ (316 K). True.
Statement II: p-dichlorobenzene (m.p. 326 K) packs better in the crystal than o-dichlorobenzene (m.p. 256 K), but its boiling point (447 K) is lower than that of the polar o-isomer (453 K). True.
Both statements are true.

A. In Hoffmann bromamide degradation, 4 moles of NaOH and 2 moles of $\mathrm{Br_2}$ are consumed per mole of an amide
B. Hoffmann bromamide reaction is not given by alkyl amides.

$\mathrm{C(s)+CO_2(g)\rightleftharpoons2CO(g)}\quad K_{p_2}=2$ atm
